text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The sailor's branch of the Solidarity trade union will join a Europe-wide protest against shipowners switching away from national to so-called cheap banners, and to demand regular group labour contracts. The protest is organised by the International Federation of Transport.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 5.7 percent this year but the rate will decline to 4.9 percent in 1998, a report by the Market Econonomy Research Institute said.
- Around 20 percent of Poles have never used banking services, a survey by the Pentor polling institute said.
- Around 18 million Poles lived below the minimum income level in 1996 and 1.7 million lived in poverty, a report presented to the cabinet's social and economic council showed.
- The EU Committee of Permanent Representatives (Coreper) approved Poland's March 18 report on a new system of car part imports by Korea's Daewoo for its assembly plants in Poland.

- The Finnish-Polish Fazer confectionery maker is planning to double output this year and build a new plant, Oy Karl Fazer AB president Felix Bjoerklund said. Fazer has a five 5.0 percent share in Poland's confectionery market.
- Sales of the Polish branch of the U.S.-British Vision Express optical firm were 24 million zlotys in 1996 and will double to 50 million this year, Vision Express president Dean Butler said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- A banking consortium led by Pekao SA bank has presented a 10-year 362 million zlotys development credit to the Elektrownia Laziska power plant, the bank said.
- The state-owned PKO BP bank granted 18,000 commercial credits last year, 12,000 of which were for small and medium size firms, PKO BP's deputy president Krzysztof Markowski said.
- Poland's Magna Polonia National Investment Fund (NFI) No.6 will invest up to $10 million in 16 food processing, chemical and motor industry schemes this year.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Over 20 Polish firms are exhibiting at the Polish Business Days in Brazil this week.
- Japan's Isuzu car firm has bought 35 hectares worth 7.0 million zlotys for a diesel engine plant it will build in the Katowice special economic zone.
ZYCIE

- Poland's debt by the end of 1996 was was $40.5 billion. The country owed $26.5 billion to the Paris Club and $7.7 billion to the London Club. The rest of the debt consisted of credits granted by World Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
PARKIET
- Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum (SZC) is planning to increase its stake in the Star truck plantin Starachowice, southern Poland, SZC said. The holding now controls a 28.1 percent stake in the plant.
